main_text.p: pellant) quicquid naturæ aut rationi il-lius muneris sive vocationis non est con-sentaneum. Potest enim id licere Magi-stratui politico, quod non licet verbi Ministro, aut è contra: itémque mercatori, quod non agricolæ; domino, quod non servo; conjugi, quod non cælibi; & sic de cæteris. Quibus omnibus Deus in genere legem hanc sixit, ut quisque quod suæ vocationis est fideliter faciat, intraque fines ejus modeste se contineat.[illegible, ~6 letters]

Siquis ergo mercator Anglus juraret lanas, aut alias merces extra regnum Angliæ lege deportari prohibitas Hamburgum mittere; aut si Magistratui aliquis juraret se non puniturum furtum aut adulterium; aut Episcopus vel Presbyter se nunquam concionaturum, aut Sacramenta administraturum; aut servus rusticus se domino jubenti boves jungere vel fruges demetere non pari-turum: quorum primum illud legibus regni, reliqua conditionibus propria vocationis adversantur. Essent ista omnia juramenta rei eo quo jam dixi gradu illicitæ; & ipsa etiam propterea juramenta illicita, & ordinarie non obligarent.[illegible, ~5 letters] Dico ordinarie: quia fortasse possunt dari casus, in quibus Juramen-tum

page.notes: The right-hand margin is cut off at the scan edge; its note fragments (about one line in five) cannot be read and are marked illegible at their approximate positions. The mark before "Anglus" is a small sign I could not identify; it is rendered as Anglus in black letter. The catchword "tum" is the first word of the next page, printed at the foot right. Hyphens are kept as printed at line ends. The s long s has been written as a plain s throughout.
